methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Late Stage → next-stage step-up multiplier (1.2x) to $5.0B total raised proxy.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 0 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 12 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

methods.name: Public-Comp Anchoring
methods.skip_reason: target revenue not on file (private companies rarely disclose)
methods.rationale: Public Semiconductors P/S median is 21.5x across 3 tickers. Cannot apply without target's revenue.

data.narrative:
Rapidus is a late-stage semiconductor company that has raised $5.0B+ to date. The valuation landscape for frontier chip firms includes 3 public comparables (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private peers such as Cerebras, Credo Semiconductor, and SambaNova Systems, though direct same-stage comparability remains limited.

Given data constraints, stage-progression methodology is the primary applicable valuation approach. Using total capital raised ($5.0B) as a proxy baseline and applying a 1.2x step-up multiplier typical for late-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $6.0B. Public semiconductor comps trade at a median P/S multiple of 21.5x across the three tickers identified, but this cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures—a standard limitation for private company analysis.

The triangulated range is $5.1B to $6.9B, with a midpoint of $6.0B supported by stage-progression logic alone. Key uncertainties include the absence of narrow-set peer valuations in the semiconductor frontier-tech segment, lack of revenue disclosure enabling multiple-based approaches, and limited visibility into capital efficiency relative to disclosed private competitors. The single-method derivation suggests material sensitivity to stage-progression assumptions and argues for direct revenue benchmarking or transaction data once available.
